'''Business and economy'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests]]
**Amid [[minimum wage]] protests by [[clothing industry|garment workers]], 13 [[Textile industry in Bangladesh|garment factories]] in [[Gazipur District|Gazipur]] are shut indefinitely under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 and over 50 remain closed in [[Savar Upazila|Savar]] and [[Ashulia]], while 48 [[platoon]]s of the [[Border Guard Bangladesh|Border Guard]], [[Bangladesh Ansar|Ansar]], and [[Special Response Battalion]] deploy across industrial zones in [[Dhaka District|Dhaka]], Gazipur, and [[Narayanganj District|Narayanganj]]. [https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/rmg/13-factories-shut-indefinitely-gazipur-amid-labour-unrest-holiday-declared-five-1602791 (''The Business Standard'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–Philippines relations]]
**[[Australia]] and the [[Philippines]] sign a defence cooperation agreement in [[Manila]], simplifying procedures for joint [[military exercise]]s and expanding [[maritime surveillance]], [[information sharing]], training, and [[disaster response]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/philippines-australia-sign-defence-pact-with-eye-china-2026-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Estonia–Russia relations]], [[Russian sabotage operations in Europe]]
**[[Estonia]] announces the closure of its three [[Estonia–Russia border|border crossings]] with [[Russia]] starting December 1 after eight suspects were detained over an attempted [[arson]] attack on [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]] manufacturer Threod Systems, which [[Estonian Foreign Intelligence Service|Estonian intelligence]] attributes to Russia's [[GRU (Russian Federation)|GRU]]. '''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Karak church shooting]], [[Capital punishment in Jordan]]
**The [[Jordan]]ian [[State Security Court]] sentences three men to [[Capital punishment|death]] for an October 23 [[Mass shooting|shooting]] at a [[Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem|Greek Orthodox]] church in [[Karak Governorate]] that killed nine people and injured 25 others. Two accomplices receive six-year prison sentences. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20261115-three-men-sentenced-to-death-over-jordan-church-attack (AFP via France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Cape Verdean presidential election]]
**[[Cape Verdeans]] vote to elect a [[President of Cape Verde|president]], where the main two candidates are the incumbent [[PAICV]] candidate [[José Maria Neves]] and the [[Movement for Democracy (Cape Verde)|MpD]] candidate [[Joana Rosa]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cape-verde-presidential-election-rosa-neves-b066358194132f21ea91bcbd6699d5e0 (AP)] 
**Neves wins re-election to a second five-year term with 63.8% of the vote, according to provisional results from the [[election commission]]. Rosa [[Concession (politics)|concedes]] defeat. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20261115-cape-verde-s-president-jose-maria-neves-re-elected-provisional-election-results (AFP via France 24)] [https://inforpress.cv/pt/presidenciais2026-joana-rosa-reconhece-derrota-eleitoral-e-reafirma-compromisso-com-a-democracia-e-politica (''Inforpress'' <small>in Portuguese</small>)]
*[[2026 Gagauz general election]]
**[[Gagauzians]] in [[Moldova]] vote to elect a [[Governor of Gagauzia|governor]] and 35 members of the [[People's Assembly of Gagauzia|People's Assembly]]. [[Parliament of Moldova|MP]] [[Alexandr Stoianoglo]] and {{ill|Fiodor Gagauz|ru|Гагауз, Фёдор Никодимович}} advance to the second round after no candidate received a majority of the vote. [https://radiomoldova.md/p/89743/gagauzia-voters-to-elect-governor-and-regional-assembly (''Radio Moldova'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/restive-pro-russian-moldovan-region-holds-elections-2026-11-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 WTA Finals]]
**[[2026 WTA Finals – Doubles]]
***In [[tennis]], [[Kateřina Siniaková]] and [[Taylor Townsend]] win their second and first [[WTA Finals]] [[Doubles (tennis)|doubles]] titles, respectively, after defeating [[Sara Errani]] and [[Jasmine Paolini]] in the final, 6–4, 6–3. [https://www.desertsun.com/story/sports/tennis/2026/11/15/a-doubles-double-dip-for-townsend-and-siniakova-as-bnp-champs-win-wta-finals/92801016007/ (''The Desert Sun'')]
**[[2026 WTA Finals – Singles]]
***In tennis, [[Mirra Andreeva]] wins her first WTA Finals [[Singles (tennis)|singles]] title after defeating [[Elina Svitolina]] in the final, 7–5, 6–3. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20261115-andreeva-defeats-svitolina-to-win-wta-finals (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 European Tour]]
**In [[golf]], [[Rory McIlroy]] equals [[Colin Montgomerie]]'s record for the most [[Harry Vardon Trophy|Harry Vardon Trophies]] after winning his eighth [[Race to Dubai]] title, which McIlroy claimed after finishing second at the [[DP World Tour Championship]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20261115-mcilroy-wins-record-equalling-eighth-race-to-dubai-title (AFP via France 24)]

**In [[women's rugby league]], [[Australia women's national rugby league team|Australia]] wins its fourth consecutive [[Women's Rugby League World Cup|World Cup]] title after defeating [[New Zealand women's national rugby league team|New Zealand]] 34–10 in the final in [[Brisbane]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20261115-australia-crush-new-zealand-34-10-to-win-women-s-rugby-league-world-cup (AFP via RFI)]

**In [[association football]], [[England national football team|England]] defeats [[Spain national football team|Spain]] 3–2 in the [[group stage]] of [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League A|UEFA Nations League A]] to end Spain's 43-match [[unbeaten streak]], the [[List of world association football records#Longest streaks|longest]] by a [[national team]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nations-league-england-spain-kane-france-7e32be3d9b49ad4d7f6ed0b59ca7410c (AP)]

**In [[Canadian football]], the [[Edmonton Elks]] win their 15th [[Canadian Football League]] title after beating the [[Montreal Alouettes]] 37–30 in the [[Grey Cup]]. They previously won in [[103rd Grey Cup|2015]]. [https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/football/cfl/edmonton-elks/edmonton-elks-grey-cup-montreal-alouettes (''Edmonton Journal'')]
